Alice / Bob —

Thanks — attached is the initial cost model (Acme_cost_model_v1.xlsx) and a short SOC2 evidence request checklist (SOC2_evidence_request.pdf) to help your security team scope the review. High-level summary below to make the numbers easy to scan: 

Assumptions: baseline 200M tokens / month (we included a +50% scenario at 300M). Estimates include generation tokens only; if you have heavy embedding/ingest volumes we can add a separate tab.

1) Hosted API (fastest to start)
- Price (example): $0.12 per 1k generated tokens
- Monthly cost @200M tokens: 200,000 * $0.12 = $24,000/month
- Pros: no infra commitments, instant scale, Redwood-managed security controls (SOC2), built-in analytics.
- Cons: higher unit cost at sustained high volume, less network-level isolation.

2) Dedicated (reserved capacity) — 3 example tiers (monthly commit + effective per-token at ~70% util):
- Small commit: $35,000/month commit -> effective per-1k token ~$0.06 @200M
- Medium commit: $65,000/month commit -> effective per-1k token ~$0.035 @200M
- Large commit: $120,000/month commit -> effective per-1k token ~$0.018 @200M
- Notes: Effective per-token assumes steady utilization and benefits from lower model/infra unit cost. Dedicated gives GPU isolation, SLA-backed throughput, and lower variable spend when fully utilized. We included burst/overage pricing in sheet.

3) Private (VPC / on-prem) — ballpark
- One-time setup & license: ~$200k (on-prem option higher depending on hardware)
- Recurring support & maintenance: ~$25k/month
- Pros: full network isolation, can meet strict procurement/legal requirements.
- Cons: longer lead time, higher upfront cost, ops responsibility (unless we bundle managed services).

Hybrid path we often recommend: start on Hosted for pilot (low friction), move to Dedicated reserved for production throughput once volumes and SLOs stabilize. Private is reserved for regulated customers with strict contracts.

Requested from you to finalize the model:
- Finalized token forecast (200M vs. 300M) and expected utilization shape (steady vs spiky).
- Any required region restrictions beyond US.
- List of procurement stakeholders (we can include them on a pricing call).

Marissa — can you and the SE team review the capacity numbers in the spreadsheet before the call? I'll leave the deck with the detailed GPU-sizing notes in the Drive link.
